ex.en: Working with your hands is seen as almost a mark of inferiority.
ex.zh: 用双手工作几乎被看作是低下的表现。

ex.en: A constant diet of criticism can leave children with a deep sense of inferiority.
ex.zh: 持续的批评会让儿童产生深深的自卑感。

ex.en: He overcame his feelings of inferiority by mastering skills his classmates lacked.
ex.zh: 他通过掌握同学们不具备的技能克服了自卑感。

ex.en: The study links constant social comparison online to feelings of inferiority.
ex.zh: 该研究表明，持续的网络社会比较与自卑感有关。

senses: adj. 极大的；无法衡量的
infinite.usage: 反义词：finite有限的。；【记】宇宙是无限的。反finite a.有限的；adj.无限的，无边的；无穷大的； 非限定的 n.无穷大；adj.无限的，无穷尽的；极大的； 非限定的；in(表示"不")+fin(范围)+ite(形容词后缀)→没有范围的→无限的；索引p410

ex.en: Not only are the tasks apparently infinite, the co-workers are much harder to motivate.
ex.zh: 不仅仅是任务似乎无穷无尽，而且激发同事的积极性也要困难得多。

ex.en: Space appears to be infinite, stretching far beyond what our telescopes can see.
ex.zh: 太空似乎无穷无尽，延伸到远远超出我们望远镜所能看见的地方。

ex.en: A good teacher knows that a child's curiosity is almost infinite.
ex.zh: 一位好老师知道孩子的好奇心几乎是无穷的。

senses: adj. (身体上)虚弱的,(心理上)脆弱的
infirm.usage: adj.体弱多病的；软弱的；adj.体弱多病的

senses: vt. 抬高（物价）；使（通货）膨胀
vt.&vi. （使）充气，（使）膨胀；使（价格、成本等）上涨
inflate.usage: in-（进入）+flat（吹）→吹入气→膨胀。反义：deflate v. 放气；紧缩；v.（使）充气，膨胀；使（价格） 上涨；夸大，吹嘘；索引p410

ex.en: The three-fifths formula handed Jefferson his narrow victory in the presidential election of 1800 by inflating the votes of the southern states in the Electoral College.
ex.zh: 五分之三代表权的规定增加了选举团中南方各州的选票数，从而使杰斐逊在1800年的总统选举中以微弱的优势胜出。

ex.en: You will need a small pump to inflate the air mattress before use.
ex.zh: 使用前你需要用一个小气泵给充气床垫充气。

ex.en: Sellers sometimes inflate the prices of goods just before major holidays.
ex.zh: 卖家有时会在重大节日前抬高商品价格。

ex.en: Critics say the company inflated its earnings reports to attract investors.
ex.zh: 批评者说，该公司夸大盈利报告以吸引投资者。

senses: n. 通货膨胀；膨胀；抬高；抬升
inflation.usage: [反] deflation n. 通货紧缩；反义词：deflation通货紧缩。；in（表示"否定"）+flat（公寓）+ion（名词后缀）→公寓都住不起了，因为"通货膨胀"了；拓展：cosmic inflation 宇宙膨胀说；词根记忆：in(向内)+flat(blow,吹)+ion(名词后缀)→向内吹气使其膨胀→通

ex.en: Their purchasing power has dropped markedly with inflation.
ex.zh: 随着通货膨胀，他们的购买力显著下降。

ex.en: This year's rise, an average of 2.7 percent, may be a fraction lower than last year's, but it is still well above the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) measure of inflation.
ex.zh: 今年(英国铁路票价)平均涨幅为2.7%，也许比去年的涨幅小一些，但仍远高于官方用消费者物价指数(CPI)衡量的通货膨胀率。

ex.en: The central bank raised interest rates in an effort to control inflation.
ex.zh: 央行为控制通货膨胀而上调了利率。

senses: adj. 膨胀的；通货膨胀的
inflationary.usage: adj.通货膨胀的；引起通货膨胀 的；索引p410

senses: adj. 僵化的；固守己见的；不可弯曲的
inflexible.usage: 真 inflexible policy 政策僵化；索引p410

senses: vt. 予以（打击）；使遭受（损伤、苦痛等）
v. (on/upon sb./sth.) 使遭受打击,使吃苦头
n. 影响；有影响力的人/事物
influence.usage: in-(进入)+flu(流)→流入其中→影响；[族] influential a. 有影响力的；influence多指潜移默化的影响；effect泛指效果、结果。；【记】父母对孩子的影响很大。近affect vt.影响；词根：in(into进入)+flu(flow流动)+ence名词后缀→流入→影响；索引p410

ex.en: Parents' words and behaviors have a great influence on their children.
ex.zh: 父母的言行对孩子有很大的影响。

ex.en: In this as in much else, those who wish to influence the future must prepare for it.
ex.zh: 在这方面，以及和其他无数种情况一样，那些希望影响未来的人们必须为此做好准备。

ex.en: It now appears that they also have an important influence on the geophysical processes.
ex.zh: 现在看来，它们好像还对地球物理过程有重要影响。

ex.en: It argues that since prosecutors do not consume a company's products as part of their investigations, they could be influenced only by the halo effect.
ex.zh: 它（指这项研究）表明，由于检察官不会将消费某公司的产品当作其调查的一部分，他们可能只受到光环效应的影响。

senses: adj. 有影响的，有势力的
influential.usage: adj.有影响力的，有势力的 n.有影响力的人；索引p410

ex.en: Instead, the studies ended up giving their name to the "Hawthorne effect," the extremely influential idea that the very act of being experimented upon changed subjects' behavior.
ex.zh: 相反，这些研究最终以“霍桑效应”命名，这是一种极其有影响力的观点，即对受试者进行实验的行为本身改变了受试者的行为。

ex.en: She is one of the most influential writers in modern American literature.
ex.zh: 她是现代美国文学中最有影响力的作家之一。

ex.en: A small group of influential politicians pushed the reform through parliament.
ex.zh: 一小群有影响力的政客推动改革在议会获得通过。

senses: v. ①(of,about) 通知，告诉，报告

phrases.p: inform the international students about an upcoming singing contest
phrases.m: 通知国际学生即将举行歌唱比赛

inform.usage: inform sb. of sth.注意of搭配，不用双宾语。；【记】请随时告知我你的决定。派information n.信息；信息（information）是我们了解（inform）的东西；拓展：well-informed 消息灵通的；ill-informed 消息不灵通的；词根：in(into进入)+form(表格

ex.en: Please inform us of any changes of address.
ex.zh: 地址若有变动请通知我们。

ex.en: Ideally, different kinds of reading inform each other, and act as useful reference points for and counterbalances to one another.
ex.zh: 理想的情况是，不同的阅读方式相互影响、互为参考、相互平衡。

ex.en: Customers should inform the bank immediately if their cards are lost or stolen.
ex.zh: 银行卡遗失或被盗，客户应立即通知银行。

ex.en: These interviews informed the design of the final questionnaire.
ex.zh: 这些访谈为最终问卷的设计提供了依据。

senses: adj. 非正式的(言行),轻松随意的,非正规的,休闲的
adj. 非正式的，不拘礼节的
adj. 非正式的；非正规的

ex.en: The interview was surprisingly informal, conducted over coffee rather than across a desk.
ex.zh: 面试出人意料地随意，是在喝咖啡时进行的，而不是隔着办公桌。

ex.en: Much valuable learning takes place through informal conversations among colleagues.
ex.zh: 许多有价值的学习是通过同事之间非正式的交谈进行的。

ex.en: Avoid slang and informal expressions in academic writing.
ex.zh: 在学术写作中应避免俚语和非正式的表达。

senses: n. [U] 消息；信息；情报；资料

phrases.p: a vast storehouse of digital information
phrases.m: 一个庞大的数字数据库

information.usage: 【记】这些信息很有价值。；词根：in(into进入)+form(表格)+ation名词后缀→填进表格，成为信息；索引p410

ex.en: This week, it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade.
ex.zh: 本周，它（指美国联邦贸易委员会）向美国五家最有价值的科技公司询问了关于它们在过去十年中进行的许多小规模收购的信息。

ex.en: The internet gives patients instant access to medical information.
ex.zh: 互联网让病人可以即时获取医疗信息。

ex.en: Officials refused to release any information about the ongoing negotiation.
ex.zh: 官员们拒绝透露有关正在进行的谈判的任何信息。

senses: n. 基础设施；基础建设
n. [C,U] 基础设施；基础建设
n. (国家或机构的)基础设施,基础建设
n. 基础设施，基础建设
n. (国家或机构的)基础设施
infrastructure.usage: infra-（在下）+structure（结构）→下面的结构→基础设施。近义：facility n. 设施；【记】政府加大了基础设施建设的投资。；n.基础设施，基础建设；辨析：infrastructure指基础建设和服务，也可抽象指政党的基础结构；facility指为特定目的提供的建筑、设备或服务；索引p410

ex.en: The sensible place to build new houses, factories and offices is where people are, in cities and towns where infrastructure is in place.
ex.zh: 建造新房屋、工厂、办公室的理想场所是人口众多之地,在基础设施完善的城市和城镇中。

ex.en: The infrastructure required to make a physical newspaper—printing presses, delivery trucks—isn't just expensive; it's excessive at a time when online-only competitors don't have the same set of financial constraints.
ex.zh: 制作一份实体报纸所需的基础设施——印刷机、送货卡车——不仅昂贵；而且贵得过分，当下只做网络报纸的竞争对手没有同样的财务限制。

ex.en: The government plans to invest billions in the country's aging transport infrastructure.
ex.zh: 政府计划在该国老化的交通基础设施上投入数十亿资金。

senses: adj. 不经常发生的；罕见的
v. 注入(某种特性);泡(茶);泡制(草药)
infuse.usage: v.使充满，灌输；冲泡； 输注

senses: a. 精巧的；心灵手巧的
adj. ①(人、头脑)灵巧的，机灵的
②(主意等)别出心裁的；巧妙的
adj. 巧妙的；心灵手巧的；机敏的；善于创造发明的；精巧的
ingenious.usage: 【记】这是一个巧妙的设计。；ingenious 有独创性，强调创造能力；clever 聪明机灵，暗示身体灵巧或思维敏捷；cunning 巧妙狡猾；adj.灵巧的，有独创性的；精巧 的，巧妙的；天才（genius）一般也是机灵的（ingenious）

ex.en: She's very ingenious when it comes to finding excuses.
ex.zh: 她很善于找借口。

ex.en: She devised an ingenious device that waters the plants while the family is away.
ex.zh: 她设计出一个精巧的装置，能在全家外出期间给植物浇水。

ex.en: The escape plan was so ingenious that the guards never suspected a thing.
ex.zh: 越狱计划如此巧妙，看守们毫无察觉。

ex.en: Farmers devised an ingenious method of collecting rainwater for the dry season.
ex.zh: 农民们想出了一种巧妙的收集雨水以备旱季的方法。

senses: n. 心灵手巧；足智多谋；巧妙
n. 心灵手巧,足智多谋;独创性
ingenuity.usage: 源自ingenious（机灵的，巧妙的）。；源于 ingenious a. 巧妙的。近义：creativity n. 创造力

ex.en: The bridge is a triumph of engineering ingenuity.
ex.zh: 这座桥是工程独创性的一个杰作。

ex.en: Faced with a shortage of parts, local mechanics showed great ingenuity.
ex.zh: 面对零件短缺，当地机械师展现出了极大的巧思。

ex.en: Human ingenuity will find ways to adapt to a warming planet.
ex.zh: 人类的聪明才智会找到办法适应变暖的地球。

senses: n. 成分，要素，因素；材料
ingredient.usage: ingredient指混合物的组成成分；element指要素、元素。；【记】面粉是做面包的主要原料。近element n.要素；in(里面)+gredi(搁点)+ent(进去)→做饭时往菜里面放点材料→材料；索引p410

ex.en: The ingredients of the product are listed on the package.
ex.zh: 产品的成分都列在包装上。

ex.en: Investors now view stock-market swings as a necessary ingredient to a sustained boom.
ex.zh: 投资者现在认为股市波动是持续繁荣的必要因素。

ex.en: Trust is an essential ingredient in any successful business partnership.
ex.zh: 信任是任何成功商业合作的要素。

ex.en: Flour, water and salt are the basic ingredients of bread.
ex.zh: 面粉、水和盐是面包的基本原料。

senses: v. 居住于，（动物）栖居于
vt. 占据；居住在；栖息于
inhabit.usage: inhabit及物动词，直接接地点；live in+地点。；【记】这个地区居住着许多珍稀动物。派inhabitant n.居民；in（里面）+habit（习惯）→人一般都习惯居住在家里→居住于，栖息于。；索引p410

ex.en: Mammals, such as dolphins, whales, seals inhabit the sea.
ex.zh: 像海豚、鲸、海豹之类的哺乳动物均栖息于大海之中。

ex.en: Everybody wants to know how the people who will soon inhabit those empty office cubicles will differ from those who came before them.
ex.zh: 所有人都想知道，这些即将很快占据那些办公室隔间空位的人与之前的人有什么不同。

ex.en: Tiny organisms inhabit even the harshest deserts, surviving on almost no water.
ex.zh: 即使在最严酷的沙漠里也栖息着微小的生物，它们几乎不靠水就能存活。

ex.en: Nearly a third of the species inhabiting the reef are found nowhere else.
ex.zh: 栖息在这片珊瑚礁的物种中，近三分之一是别处没有的。

senses: n. 居民，居住者；栖息动物
inhabitant.usage: 【记】这个城市的居民很友好。；索引p410

ex.en: We will try to give cheap electric energy and heat to every inhabitant of the world.
ex.zh: 我们努力向全世界每位居民提供廉价的电能和热能。

ex.en: Early inhabitants of the island lived mainly by fishing and trading.
ex.zh: 岛上的早期居民主要靠捕鱼和贸易为生。

ex.en: The new metro line will cut journey times for more than a million inhabitants.
ex.zh: 新地铁线路将缩短一百多万居民的出行时间。

ex.en: The remote valley's few inhabitants still travel mainly on foot or by horse.
ex.zh: 这个偏远山谷的少数居民出行仍主要靠步行或骑马。

senses: v. 吸入（空气、烟雾或气体等）
adj. 固有的,内在的,天生的
inherent.usage: 词根记忆：in(in,在里面)+her(stick,粘)+ent→黏在基因里的→固有的。；索引p410

ex.en: Individuality is a valued and inherent part of the British character.
ex.zh: 个性是英国人重视并固有的特征。

ex.en: the inherent worth of each individual
ex.zh: 每一个个体的内在价值

ex.en: Risk is inherent in every investment, however safe it appears.
ex.zh: 无论一项投资看起来多么安全，风险都是其固有的。

senses: v. 继承（财产、传统等）；经遗传获得
v. 继承，经遗传获得；接替；继任
vt. 继承(金钱、财产等)；经遗传获得(品质、身体特征等)；继任
inherit.usage: inherit sth. from sb.从某人处继承某物。；【记】他继承了父亲的遗产。派inheritance n.继承；遗产；他想让儿子继承(inherit)他的遗产(heritage)。；词根记忆：in(in,在里面)+her(heir,继承)+it→继承。；索引p410

ex.en: She inherited a fortune from her father.
ex.zh: 她从她父亲那里继承了一大笔财富。

ex.en: inherit wealth
ex.zh: 世袭财富

ex.en: Children may inherit their parents' eye colour and some of their character traits.
ex.zh: 孩子可能继承父母的眼睛颜色和部分性格特征。

senses: adj. 继承的,通过继承取得的
vt. 使某人不能做轻易可做的事
vt. 阻碍或抑制(某过程或行动)
inhibit.usage: in-（进入）+hibit（拿住）→拿住不动→抑制。近义：restrain vt. 抑制；索引p410

ex.en: Fear of failure can inhibit creativity in the classroom.
ex.zh: 对失败的恐惧会抑制课堂上的创造力。

ex.en: The drug inhibits the growth of cancer cells.
ex.zh: 这种药物会抑制癌细胞的生长。

ex.en: Strict regulations may inhibit the development of small businesses.
ex.zh: 严苛的监管可能会阻碍小企业的发展。

senses: adj. 冷酷无情的,非人的,(似非人所为而)恐怖的
inhuman.usage: adj.残忍的；野蛮的；无人性 的

senses: adj. ①最初的，开始的，开头的
initial.usage: 【记】初始阶段总是最困难的。；adj.开始的，最初的；(字母)位 于词首的 n.(姓名的)首字母 v.用姓名的首字母签名于；词根记忆：in(in,里)+it(go,去)+ial(形容词后缀)→向里去的→最初的。；索引p410

ex.en: initial draft
ex.zh: 初稿

ex.en: The initial reaction to the proposal was positive, but doubts soon appeared.
ex.zh: 对该提案的最初反应是积极的，但疑问很快出现了。

ex.en: Initial reports said three people had been injured in the accident.
ex.zh: 最初的报道说事故中有三人受伤。

senses: v. 开始，发起；使初步了解

phrases.m: 把……传授给某人；接纳某人加入

initiate.usage: 辨析：initiate开始；imitate模仿；intimidate恐吓。；initi（开始）+ate→使开始→发起。族：initiative n. 主动性；倡议。近义：launch vt. 发起；v.开始，发起 n.新入会的人；in(进入)+it(走)+ate(动词后缀)→走进去→开始，发起；词根记忆：in(in,里

ex.en: The government has initiated a programme of economic reform.
ex.zh: 政府已开始实施经济改革方案。

ex.en: The most famous of these efforts was initiated by Noam Chomsky, who suggested that humans are born with an innate language-acquisition capacity that dictates a universal grammar.
ex.zh: 在这些成果中，最著名的是由诺姆·乔姆斯基首先提出的。他指出，人类生来就具有某种驾驭普遍语法的先天语言习得能力。

ex.en: The company initiated a training scheme to help new employees adapt quickly.
ex.zh: 公司启动了一项培训计划，帮助新员工快速适应。

senses: n. (常指通过特别仪式的)入会
n. 介绍某人初试某活动(或技艺);开始,创始,发起
n. (常包含特殊仪式的)入会；发起

ex.en: initiation ceremonies
ex.zh: 入会仪式

ex.en: Young warriors underwent a painful initiation before being accepted into the tribe.
ex.zh: 年轻的武士要经历痛苦的入会仪式才能被部落接纳。

ex.en: The project marked the initiation of a new era in space research.
ex.zh: 该项目标志着太空研究新时代的开端。

senses: n. 主动性；倡议；主动权
n. 主动性(权)；进取心；倡议

phrases.p: act/do sth. on one's own initiative

initiative.usage: initiate 的派生词；【记】他主动提出了这个建议。；n.措施，倡议；主动性；n.措施，倡议；主动；主动权；索引p410

ex.en: an HIV-prevention initiative
ex.zh: 一项"防艾"倡议

ex.en: propose a new initiative
ex.zh: 提出一个新方案

ex.en: individual initiative or creativity
ex.zh: 个人主动性或创造力

ex.en: institute weight loss and fitness initiatives
ex.zh: 开始减肥和健康计划

ex.en: She was the initiator of the campaign to protect the city's old libraries.
ex.zh: 她是保护该市旧图书馆运动的发起人。

ex.en: As the initiator of the reform, he faced fierce opposition from within his own party.
ex.zh: 作为这项改革的发起者，他遭到了自己党内的激烈反对。

ex.en: The initiator of the project hoped other villages would copy the model.
ex.zh: 该项目的发起人希望其他村庄能效仿这一模式。

inject.usage: 【记】医生给他注射了抗生素。派injection n.注射；in(在……里面)+ject(投,掷,射)→在里面射→注射;派生injection n.注射；v.注射；添加；投入；注入；词根词缀法：in（表示“里面”）+ject（抛，扔）→往里扔→注射。；in（里面）+ject（抛，扔）→往里扔→注射；索引p410

ex.en: The boss refused to inject any more capital into the new project.
ex.zh: 老板拒绝向新项目注入更多的资金。

ex.en: The nurse injected the vaccine into the child's left arm.
ex.zh: 护士把疫苗注射进孩子的左臂。

ex.en: A good joke can inject some humor into a dull speech.
ex.zh: 一个好笑话可以为沉闷的演讲注入一些幽默。

ex.en: The nurse gave the patient an injection to relieve the pain.
ex.zh: 护士给病人打了一针以缓解疼痛。

ex.en: A large injection of cash saved the struggling airline from bankruptcy.
ex.zh: 一大笔资金的注入使这家陷入困境的航空公司免于破产。

ex.en: Vaccination works by injecting a harmless form of the virus.
ex.zh: 疫苗接种通过注射无害形式的病毒来起作用。

senses: v. 使受伤；损害,伤害(名誉、自尊等)
v. （尤指在事故中）伤害，使受伤

phrases.m: 损害他在历史上的地位

injure.usage: 【记】他在事故中受了重伤。派injury n.伤害；损伤；v.使受伤，弄伤；损害，伤害

ex.en: Several people were seriously injured.
ex.zh: 数人受重伤。

ex.en: Three firefighters were injured while tackling the warehouse fire.
ex.zh: 三名消防员在扑救仓库大火时受了伤。

ex.en: Smoking seriously injures the lungs and raises the risk of heart disease.
ex.zh: 吸烟严重损害肺部并增加患心脏病的风险。

ex.en: He injured his back lifting heavy boxes during the move.
ex.zh: 搬家时他因搬重箱子伤了背部。

senses: adj. 造成伤害的；有害的

ex.en: Darwin was convinced that the loss of these tastes was not only a loss of happiness, but might possibly be injurious to the intellect, and more probably to the moral character.
ex.zh: 达尔文认为，这些品味的缺失，不仅是一种快乐的丧失，还可能损伤智力，甚至更可能对道德品质有害。

ex.en: Doctors warn that sugary drinks are injurious to dental health, especially in children.
ex.zh: 医生警告说，含糖饮料对牙齿健康有害，对儿童尤甚。

ex.en: Exposure to the chemical was found to be injurious to workers' eyesight.
ex.zh: 人们发现，接触这种化学物质会损害工人的视力。

ex.en: The report concluded that the additive was not injurious to health in small amounts.
ex.zh: 报告的结论是，这种添加剂少量摄入对健康无害。

injury.usage: [族]injure vt. 伤害；【记】他在事故中受了重伤。

ex.en: He was lucky to escape injury.
ex.zh: 他很幸运没有受伤。

ex.en: The striker missed the rest of the season because of a knee injury.
ex.zh: 这名前锋因膝伤缺席了本赛季余下的比赛。

ex.en: Wearing a helmet greatly reduces the risk of head injury.
ex.zh: 戴头盔能大大降低头部受伤的风险。

senses: v. 给……上油墨；签署,签订(合同等)
ink.usage: 助记:把ink(墨水)倒入sink(水槽)里

senses: adj. 国内的,内地的,内陆的
adj. 与生俱来的,天生的,固有的
innate.usage: adj.先天的，固有的；谐音记忆：发音近似"因内特"→内部的特点→天生的。；索引p410

ex.en: innate language-acquisition capacity
ex.zh: 先天语言习得能力

ex.en: Chomsky argues that humans possess an innate capacity for grammar.
ex.zh: 乔姆斯基认为人类拥有先天的语法能力。

ex.en: Some birds show an innate ability to navigate by the stars.
ex.zh: 有些鸟类表现出与生俱来的靠星星导航的本领。

inner.usage: the inner circle of power权力的核心集团

senses: adj. 最深处的,最内部的
adj. 无害的;无辜受害的,成为牺牲品的
innocent.usage: 【记】他是无辜的。反guilty a.有罪的；adj.天真的，幼稚的；清白的， 无罪的 n.天真无邪的人；无辜的人；in（无）+no（没有）+cent（分）→有人说他偷了钱，可他口袋里一分钱都没有→清白的，无罪的。；词根记忆：in(not,不)+noc(harm,伤害)+ent(形容词后缀)→没有伤害的→无罪的；无恶意

ex.en: Then it presents that connection, even among two-year-olds, between girls as not only innocent but as evidence of innocence.
ex.zh: 这样，粉色不仅呈现出少女，甚至是两岁女孩之间的共性：纯真，而且粉色本身也是纯真的证明。

ex.en: But it's not as if earlier times didn't know perpetual war, disaster and the massacre of innocents.
ex.zh: 但以前的时代并不似乎就没经历过无休止的战争、天灾人祸和滥杀无辜。

ex.en: The court finally proved that the young man was innocent of the crime.
ex.zh: 法庭最终证明这名年轻人没有犯该罪行。

innovate.usage: [族] innovation n. 创新；innovative a. 创新的；v.革新，创新；in(表加强)+nov(=new“新的”)+ate(动词后缀)→使它变得新一些→创新；革新；索引p410

ex.en: The first thing needed for innovation is a fascination with wonder.
ex.zh: 创新需要的第一件事是对未知的着迷。

ex.en: So then the problem is not really about technology, but rather, "how do we innovate our institutions and our work practices?"
ex.zh: 那么问题就不再围绕着科技了，而是“如何改革我们的制度和工作习惯？”

ex.en: Firms that fail to innovate quickly lose ground to younger, faster competitors.
ex.zh: 未能创新的公司很快就会输给更年轻、更敏捷的竞争者。

ex.en: Universities must innovate in how they teach if they are to stay relevant.
ex.zh: 大学要想保持现实相关性，就必须在教学方法上创新。

senses: n. 新方法,新技术,新思想
innovation.usage: 【记】技术创新推动经济发展。派innovate vi.创新；n.新事物，新方法；革新，创新；索引p410

ex.en: These issues all have root causes in human behavior: all require behavioral change and social innovations, as well as technological development.
ex.zh: 导致这些问题的根本原因都在于人类行为，这些问题都要求人们在行为上做出转变，对社会进行革新，同时发展技术。

ex.en: Technological innovation has completely changed the way people communicate with each other.
ex.zh: 技术创新已经彻底改变了人们相互交流的方式。

ex.en: The company encourages innovation by rewarding employees for new ideas.
ex.zh: 公司通过奖励员工的新想法来鼓励创新。

senses: adj. 富有革新精神的；革新的

phrases.m: 一位富有革新精神的思想家

senses: adj. 富有创新思想的；采用新方法的；革新的；创新的
innovative.usage: adj.革新的，新颖的；adj.革新的，新颖的；富有革新 精神的；索引p410

ex.en: The company is known for its innovative approach to product design.
ex.zh: 这家公司以创新的产品设计方法而闻名。

ex.en: Innovative teaching methods have raised standards in some of the poorest schools.
ex.zh: 创新的教学方法提高了一些最贫困学校的教学水平。

ex.en: The prize rewards innovative solutions to environmental problems.
ex.zh: 该奖项奖励针对环境问题的创新解决方案。

innovativeness.usage: n.创新性，创新精神；n.创新性；索引p410

ex.en: The firm's innovativeness stems from close cooperation with universities.
ex.zh: 该公司的创新性源于与大学的密切合作。

ex.en: Surveys measure the innovativeness of national economies each year.
ex.zh: 调查每年衡量各国经济的创新性。

ex.en: A culture of tolerating failure is essential to innovativeness.
ex.zh: 宽容失败的文化对创新精神至关重要。

innumerable.usage: 助记:in(在里面)+numerable(许多的)→无数的

senses: vt. 把(数据等)输入计算机
input.usage: 【记】输入决定输出。反output n.输出；助记:in(在里面)+put(放入)→放入到里面→输入；索引p410

ex.en: Teachers' input helped shape the new national curriculum.
ex.zh: 教师们的意见帮助塑造了新的国家课程。

ex.en: The data input by clerks is checked twice for errors.
ex.zh: 职员输入的数据要经过两次校对以查错。

ex.en: Higher productivity came from greater investment rather than extra labour input.
ex.zh: 生产率的提高源于更大的投资，而非额外的劳动投入。

inquire.usage: 【记】他打听了去车站的路。亦作enquire。派inquiry n.询问；调查；v.询问，打听；in（表示“里面”）+quire（=ask，问）→问到里面去了→询问，打听；词根记忆：in(into,加以)+quire(ask,询问)→加以询问；亦拼作 enquire

ex.en: He inquired about his client's family background.
ex.zh: 他询问了客户的家庭背景。

ex.en: One of the astonishing revelations was how little Rebekah Brooks knew of what went on in her newsroom, how little she thought to ask and the fact that she never inquired how the stories arrived.
ex.zh: 其中一个惊人的发现是：丽贝卡·布鲁克斯对发生在自己新闻编辑部的事情知之甚少，她几乎不想加以过问，实际上她也从不询问这些新闻报道的来源。

ex.en: Passengers may inquire about train times at the information desk in the main hall.
ex.zh: 乘客可在大厅的咨询处询问列车时刻。

ex.en: She inquired politely whether the gallery allowed photography.
ex.zh: 她礼貌地询问美术馆是否允许拍照。

inquiry.usage: inquire 的派生词；亦拼作 enquiry

ex.en: The government has ordered a public inquiry into the rail disaster.
ex.zh: 政府已下令对这起铁路灾难进行公开调查。

ex.en: The office handles inquiries from members of the public.
ex.zh: 该办公室处理公众的询问。

ex.en: Scientific inquiry begins with careful observation and honest recording.
ex.zh: 科学探究始于细致的观察和忠实的记录。

inquiryenquiry.usage: 助记:in(在里面)+quir(询问)+y(名词后缀)→打听,询问；索引p410

senses: adj. 无法满足的,贪得无厌的

inscribe.usage: in（往里，里面）+scribe（写）→写到里面→刻；题

ex.en: Inscribe this literary work onto a stone tablet and record it.
ex.zh: 把这幅文学作品刻在一块石碑上并记录下来。

insect.usage: in（人，向内）+sect（切割）→“昆虫”的纹理一段一段的，像被切割过→昆虫。

ex.en: On the road there is little to protect them from mud, insects, and bird droppings.
ex.zh: 在路上，几乎没有什么能保护它们免受泥土、昆虫和鸟粪的伤害。

ex.en: Many crops depend on insects for pollination.
ex.zh: 许多农作物依靠昆虫授粉。

ex.en: The farmer uses natural sprays rather than chemical insect killers.
ex.zh: 这位农民使用天然喷剂而不是化学杀虫剂。

insecure.usage: adj.缺乏信心的，无把握的；不 牢靠的；不安全的

senses: adj. 不敏感的；不顾他人感受的；无感觉的
insensitive.usage: adj.漠不关心的；麻木的；不敏 感的，反应迟钝的；索引p410

ex.en: His insensitive remarks about the victims caused public anger.
ex.zh: 他对受害者说的冷漠无情的话引起了公愤。

ex.en: Some interview questions are insensitive to cultural differences.
ex.zh: 有些面试问题没有考虑到文化差异。

ex.en: The staff were criticized as insensitive to patients' emotional needs.
ex.zh: 员工们被批评对病人的情感需求漠不关心。

insensitivity.usage: n.迟钝；无情，冷漠；不敏感；索引p410

senses: vt. 插入；嵌入；（在文章中）添加
insert.usage: in（进入）+sert（插入）→“插入”进来→插入，嵌进。

ex.en: They inserted a tube in his mouth to help him breathe.
ex.zh: 他们在他嘴里插了根导管帮助他呼吸。

ex.en: Insert the key into the lock and turn it gently.
ex.zh: 把钥匙插入锁孔，轻轻转动。

ex.en: The editor decided to insert a paragraph explaining the technical terms.
ex.zh: 编辑决定插入一段文字来解释那些术语。

senses: adj. 里面的,内部的,内幕的
adv./n. 在里面;内部,里面,内侧
inside.usage: 助记:in(在内)+side(面,侧面,边,部分)→在里面

ex.en: Corruption is an insidious disease that spreads through public institutions.
ex.zh: 腐败是一种潜伏蔓延于公共机构的隐袭恶疾。

ex.en: The insidious effects of long-term stress often go unnoticed for years.
ex.zh: 长期压力的隐性危害往往多年不被察觉。

ex.en: Critics describe the app's design as insidious, encouraging users to stay online.
ex.zh: 批评者称这款应用的设计阴险，诱使用户一直在线。

senses: n. 洞察力，理解力；洞悉，了解
insight.usage: 【记】这本书使我对人性有了深刻的认识。派insightful a.有深刻见解的；助记:in(向内)+sight(视力,看见,视野)→见识；n.洞悉，了解；洞察力；in(往里)+sight(看)→往里看→洞悉，了解；词根记忆：in(在…内)+sight(视野)→内在的视野→洞察力；索引p410

ex.en: Many first-generation students lack insight about why they are struggling and do not understand how students "like them" can improve.
ex.zh: 许多第一代大学生看不透为什么他们在苦苦挣扎，也不明白"像他们"这样的学生如何才能提升。

ex.en: The insight that curiosity can drive you to do self-destructive things is a profound one.
ex.zh: 好奇心可以驱使你做自取灭亡的事，这一领悟发人深省。

ex.en: Her book offers fresh insight into the causes of the financial crisis.
ex.zh: 她的书对金融危机的成因提供了新的深刻见解。

senses: a. 有深刻了解的；富有洞察力的
adj. 有深刻了解的,富有洞察力的
adj. 有深刻了解的；富有洞察力的
insightful.usage: adj.富有洞察力的，有深刻见解 的；索引p410

ex.en: The professor made several insightful comments on the students' research proposals.
ex.zh: 教授对学生的研究计划提出了几条富有洞察力的意见。

ex.en: Her insightful analysis of the election surprised even experienced political reporters.
ex.zh: 她对这次选举的深刻分析连经验丰富的政治记者都感到惊讶。

ex.en: The book is full of insightful observations about modern city life.
ex.zh: 这本书充满了对现代城市生活的深刻观察。

senses: a. 不重要的；微不足道的
insignificant.usage: adj.微不足道的，无足轻重的；索引p410

ex.en: At first the error seemed insignificant, but it later cost the company millions.
ex.zh: 起初这个错误似乎微不足道，但后来让公司损失了数百万。

ex.en: No detail is insignificant when you are designing a safety system.
ex.zh: 设计安全系统时，任何细节都不是小事。

ex.en: Compared with the vastness of the universe, human concerns can feel insignificant.
ex.zh: 与浩瀚的宇宙相比，人类的种种操心显得微不足道。

senses: vi. (on)坚决要求,坚决主张,坚持
insist.usage: 【记】他坚持要自己付账。派insistence n.坚持；助记:in(在内,在里)+sist(立)→一直站在里面→坚持；v.坚持，坚决要求；坚称；索引p410

ex.en: We're doing everything but insist that manufacturers clean up their cars.
ex.zh: 能做的我们都做了，就是没有坚持让汽车制造商生产的汽车更环保。

ex.en: She insisted that the refund be paid immediately, citing the consumer protection law.
ex.zh: 她援引消费者保护法，坚决要求立即退款。

ex.en: Officials insist that the water supply meets all safety standards.
ex.zh: 官员们坚持认为供水符合所有安全标准。

ex.en: He insisted on paying for the meal despite our protests.
ex.zh: 尽管我们一再推辞，他还是坚持要付餐费。

senses: n. 坚决要求,坚持,固执
insistence.usage: n.坚决要求，坚持主张；索引p410

ex.en: The major reason for listing the lesser prairie chicken as threatened is the insistence of private landowners.
ex.zh: 将小草原榛鸡列入"受威胁物种"名单的主要原因是私人土地所有者的坚持。

ex.en: At her insistence, the meeting was moved to a date convenient for everyone.
ex.zh: 在她的坚持下，会议改到了对大家都方便的日期。

ex.en: The minister's insistence on absolute loyalty alarmed senior officials.
ex.zh: 部长对绝对忠诚的坚决要求令高级官员们感到不安。

inspect.usage: 记：in-(进入)+spect(看)→进入车间查看产品质量→检查；[族]inspection n.检查；[近]examine vt.仔细检查；【记】官员视察了这家工厂。派inspection n.检查；视察；助记:in(向内)+spect(看)→向内看→视察,检查；v.检查，审视；检阅，视察；in（里面）+spect（

ex.en: inspect infrastructure
ex.zh: 检查基础设施

ex.en: Make sure you inspect the goods before signing for them.
ex.zh: 要确保在签收货物之前进行检验。

ex.en: Officials inspect food factories regularly to make sure safety standards are met.
ex.zh: 官员定期检查食品工厂，以确保达到安全标准。

senses: n. 视察,检查,查看,审视

ex.en: The architect is carrying out a thorough inspection of the building.
ex.zh: 建筑师正在对大楼进行全面检查。

ex.en: All imported meat is subject to strict inspection at the port.
ex.zh: 所有进口肉类都要在港口接受严格检查。

ex.en: The factory passed its annual safety inspection without a single violation.
ex.zh: 这家工厂通过了年度安全检查，没有发现任何违规。

ex.en: A routine customs inspection uncovered the smuggled goods hidden in the cargo.
ex.zh: 一次例行海关检查发现了藏在货物中的走私品。

ex.en: An inspector was sent to the scene of the incident.
ex.zh: 一名检查员被派到了事发现场。

senses: n. 灵感；鼓舞人心的人或物；好主意
n. 鼓舞；启发灵感的人(或事物)；灵感

ex.en: Both poets drew their inspiration from the countryside.
ex.zh: 两位诗人都从乡村得到他们的灵感。

ex.en: Her courage has been an inspiration to women entering science.
ex.zh: 她的勇气一直激励着进入科学领域的女性。

ex.en: The architect found inspiration in the traditional wooden houses of the region.
ex.zh: 这位建筑师从该地区传统的木屋中获得了灵感。

phrases.p: inspire astronomers to explore the heavens
phrases.m: 激励天文学家们去探寻天空

inspire.usage: 【记】老师的话激励着他前进。派inspiration n.灵感；鼓舞；adj.鼓舞人心的，有激励作用的；in（里面）+spir（呼吸）+e→往里呼吸就是打气→激励，鼓励；词根记忆：in(into,进入)+spir(breathe,呼吸)+e→给别人打气→激励；辨：expire指期满到期、死亡；索引p410

ex.en: As a teacher, she has inspired generations of students.
ex.zh: 作为一名教师，她激励了一代又一代的学生。

ex.en: Well-enforced laws in government transparency are needed to inspire hopes in average people.
ex.zh: 我们需要贯彻落实政府透明度方面的法律来使普通民众产生希望。

ex.en: The success of the first female astronaut inspired many girls to study science.
ex.zh: 第一位女宇航员的成功激励了许多女孩学习科学。

install.usage: 【记】技术人员正在安装新设备。派installation n.安装；装置

installation.usage: 助记:install(安装)+ation(名词后缀)→安装；索引p410

senses: n. （报章连载小说的）一节；（分期付款的）一期付款；（电视连续剧的）一集

phrases.p: write a story in monthly installments

installment.usage: 书中亦作instalment；词根记忆：in(里面)+stal(place, 放置)+ment(名词后缀)→放到里面的某个位置→某个部分；索引p410

senses: n. (故事分段连载或连播等的)一集

phrases.p: pay for a house by monthly instalments

instance.usage: 【记】举个例子，许多人喜欢在线阅读。近example n.例子；又:at the instance of应……之请；n.例子，实例 v.举……为例；串词记忆：脑海里立即(instant)想到一个例子(instance)；索引p410

ex.en: In some instances, remote workers report higher productivity than office staff.
ex.zh: 在某些情况下，远程员工的工作效率高于办公室员工。

ex.en: The court cited this case as an instance of blatant disregard for the law.
ex.zh: 法院援引此案作为公然无视法律的一个实例。

ex.en: For instance, a small delay in shipping can ruin a seasonal product launch.
ex.zh: 例如，运输上的一点延误就可能毁掉一件季节性产品的发布。

senses: adj. 紧急的,急迫的,立即的,即刻的
adj. (食品)已配制好的,速成的,方便的
instant.usage: 【记】他立刻就明白了。派instantly ad.立即地；同义:urgent,prompt,immediate;派生instantly立即；in(表示"里面")+stant(=stand表示"站")→站在里面，她走出来时可以"立刻，马上"迎接她→立刻的

ex.en: People today seem to want instant gratification.
ex.zh: 今天的人们似乎想要即时满足。

ex.en: The noodles are popular with students because they are an instant meal.
ex.zh: 这种面条深受学生欢迎，因为它是速食餐。

ex.en: At that instant the lights went out and the theatre fell silent.
ex.zh: 就在那一刻，灯光熄灭，剧场一片寂静。

senses: adj. 瞬间发生的,即刻的

ex.en: Modern sensors give an almost instantaneous response to changes in temperature.
ex.zh: 现代传感器对温度变化几乎能即时作出反应。

ex.en: The reaction is instantaneous once the two chemicals meet.
ex.zh: 这两种化学物质一接触，反应立即发生。

ex.en: Online shopping has trained consumers to expect almost instantaneous delivery.
ex.zh: 网购让消费者习惯了期待几乎即时送达。

ex.en: Some people told the truth instantly.
ex.zh: 一些人立即说出了真相。

instinct.usage: 【记】鸟儿筑巢是出于本能。派instinctive a.本能的；n.本能，天性；直觉；发音类似鹰死盯他→出于本能的警觉，鹰死死地盯着他→本能，直觉；词根记忆：in(内)+stinct(看作sting，刺，刺激)→内在的刺激→本能；索引p410

ex.en: Children do not know by instinct the difference between right and wrong.
ex.zh: 儿童并非生来就会分辨是非。

ex.en: When people place their trust in an individual or an institution, their brains release oxytocin, a hormone that produces pleasurable feelings and triggers the herding instinct that prompts humans to connect with one another.
ex.zh: 当人们信任一个人或者一个机构时，他们的大脑会释放出催产素，这是一种使人产生愉悦感的荷尔蒙，还会激发人类的群居本能，促使人们互相联系。

ex.en: Birds build nests by instinct, without any teaching from their parents.
ex.zh: 鸟儿凭本能筑巢，不需要父母的任何教导。

senses: adv. 本能地；凭直觉；自然而然地
n. 学会,协会,学院,研究院
institute.usage: 【记】他在这所学院任教。；in（进入）+stitut（=stand“站，建立”）+e→站进去→进入建立的状态→制定；建立。；vt.制定例为2018年翻译；索引p410

ex.en: And so he reads—everything from encyclopaedias to science fiction novels. He reads so passionately that his parents have to institute a "no reading policy" at the dinner table.
ex.zh: 所以他博览群书——从百科全书到科幻小说，所有的书他都看。他是如此地沉迷于阅读，以至于他的父母不得不制定一个在饭桌上"不许阅读的政策"。

ex.en: She works at a research institute that studies climate change.
ex.zh: 她在一家研究气候变化的研究所工作。

ex.en: The school instituted a new rule to limit students' use of mobile phones.
ex.zh: 学校制定了一项新规定，限制学生使用手机。

institution.usage: 【记】大学是重要的社会机构。；n.机构；收容机构；制度，习 俗；②n.体制例为2009年翻译，跨前页；索引p410

ex.en: It may be said that the measure of the worth of any social institution is its effect in enlarging and improving experience, but this effect is not a part of its original motive.
ex.zh: 或许可以说，衡量任何社会制度价值的标准在于其对丰富和完善人生经验所起的作用，但这种作用并非该制度原始动机的一部分。

ex.en: Marriage remains an important social institution in many countries.
ex.zh: 在许多国家，婚姻仍然是一种重要的社会制度。

ex.en: The bank is one of the oldest financial institutions in the city.
ex.zh: 这家银行是该市最古老的金融机构之一。

senses: adj. 机构的;慈善机构的;由来已久的
adj. 机构的；慈善机构的
institutional.usage: adj.机构的；制度的；根深蒂 固的；adj.机构例为2008年阅读；索引p410

ex.en: There is the so-called big deal, where institutional subscribers pay for access to a collection of online journal titles through site-licensing agreements.
ex.zh: 第一种是所谓的大订单模式，即机构用户通过签订网站许可协议的方式付费访问一系列在线期刊。

ex.en: Racism can be institutional, built into rules rather than open behaviour.
ex.zh: 种族歧视可以是制度性的，藏在规则之中而非公开行为里。

ex.en: The elderly are increasingly cared for in institutional settings rather than by relatives.
ex.zh: 老年人越来越多地由机构照护，而不是由亲属照料。

instruct.usage: 记：in-(加强)+struct(建造)→工程师向工人说明建房方案→指导；[族]instructor n.教练导师；instructive a.富有教益的；【记】医生吩咐他多休息。派instruction n.指示；教导；助记:in(在里面)+struct(建造)→在心里建造→教；v.指示，吩咐；教授，指导；词根记忆:

ex.en: instruct children
ex.zh: 教授儿童

ex.en: In one series of studies, researchers instructed Chicago-area commuters using public transportation to strike up a conversation with someone near them.
ex.zh: 在一系列研究中，研究人员让芝加哥地区乘坐公共交通工具的通勤者主动与其周围的人攀谈。

ex.en: The judge instructed the jury to consider only the evidence presented in court.
ex.zh: 法官指示陪审团只考虑在法庭上出示的证据。

ex.en: The manual instructs users to unplug the appliance before cleaning it.
ex.zh: 手册指示用户在清洁电器前先拔掉插头。

senses: n. [C] 常用pl. 指示；命令
instruction.usage: 记：in-(加强)+struct(建造)+-ion→工程师给出的建房方案→指示；[族]instructional a.教学的；[近]order n.指示命令；【记】请按照说明服药。；助记:instruct(教)+ion(名词后缀)→教授,教育；n.用法说明；指示，指令；指导；索引p410

ex.en: adapt instruction to children
ex.zh: 使教学适合儿童

ex.en: Before operating the machine, read the safety instructions printed on the panel.
ex.zh: 操作机器前，请阅读面板上印着的安全说明。

ex.en: Clear instruction from the coach helped the beginners master the basic strokes quickly.
ex.zh: 教练清晰的指导帮助初学者很快掌握了基本划水动作。

ex.en: Pupils receiving one-to-one instruction progress far faster in mathematics.
ex.zh: 接受一对一教学的小学生在数学上进步快得多。

senses: a. 富有教益的；增长知识的
adj. 有启发性的；有教育意义的

instructor.usage: n.教练，导师；大学讲师；索引p410

instrument.usage: 记：in-(内)+stru(结构)+-ment→内部结构精密的器物→仪器；[族]instrumental a.用乐器演奏的；[近]device n.仪器器具；【记】他会弹奏好几种乐器。；助记:instru(instruct教育,指导)+ment(名词后缀)→工具,仪器；n.乐器；仪器；工具

ex.en: measuring instruments
ex.zh: 测量仪器

ex.en: With creativity, even old-fashioned instruments may produce spectacular sound effects.
ex.zh: 有了创造力，即使是老式乐器也能产生令人惊叹的音效。

ex.en: The telescope is the most powerful scientific instrument of its kind ever built.
ex.zh: 这台望远镜是有史以来建造的同类型中最强大的科学仪器。

ex.en: The surgeon selected the appropriate instrument before making the incision.
ex.zh: 外科医生在开刀前选好了合适的器械。

senses: adj. 有帮助的,起作用的
adv. 有助益地；用乐器演奏地
adj. 不充分的;不够的;不足的
insufficient.usage: adj.不充分的，不够重要的；索引p411

ex.en: The bridge collapsed because insufficient funds had been spent on maintenance.
ex.zh: 这座桥倒塌是因为维护资金投入不足。

ex.en: Insufficient sleep among teenagers is linked to poor exam performance.
ex.zh: 青少年睡眠不足与考试成绩不佳有关。

ex.en: The case was dropped for insufficient evidence.
ex.zh: 该案因证据不足而被撤销。

senses: vt. 隔音,使绝缘(以免受到影响)
v. 使绝缘，使隔热，使隔音；隔离
vt. 使绝缘，使隔热，使隔音；隔离
insulate.usage: 派生insulation绝缘,隔离;insulator绝缘体,隔音(热)物；insul(岛屿)+ate(动词后缀)→像岛屿般与世隔绝→隔离；索引p411

ex.en: Home owners are being encouraged to insulate their homes to save energy.
ex.zh: 当局鼓励房主在住房加装隔热装置以节约能源。

ex.en: The wires are insulated with rubber to prevent electric shocks.
ex.zh: 电线用橡胶绝缘以防触电。

ex.en: Children of the wealthy are often insulated from the consequences of failure.
ex.zh: 富人家的孩子常常被隔绝于失败的后果之外。

senses: n. 侮辱,凌辱;损伤,危害

phrases.m: 在伤害之外又加以侮辱;雪上加霜;更糟的是

insult.usage: 【记】他因辱骂警察被罚款。；同义offend,humiliate;反义respect；千万别冒犯（insult）他，不然没有好结果（result）。

ex.en: Emma Marris' article is an insult and a disservice to the thousands of passionate people.
ex.zh: 艾玛·马里斯的文章是对成千上万热情人士的侮辱和伤害。

ex.en: Calling the report worthless is an insult to the researchers who spent years on it.
ex.zh: 说这份报告一文不值，是对为此付出了多年心血的研究人员的侮辱。

ex.en: He insulted his colleagues by questioning their honesty in public.
ex.zh: 他当众质疑同事的诚实，侮辱了他们。

senses: n. 保险,保险费,保险业
insurance.usage: assurance 的近义词；【记】他给汽车上了保险。；n.保险；保险费；预防措施；insure 的派生词；拓展: health/medical insurance 健康/医疗保险；索引p411

ex.en: Drivers must buy car insurance before they can legally drive on public roads.
ex.zh: 司机必须购买汽车保险才能合法在公共道路上行驶。

ex.en: The insurance company refused to pay because the damage was not covered by the policy.
ex.zh: 保险公司拒绝赔付，因为损失不在保单范围之内。

ex.en: Travel insurance is a wise investment for anyone planning a trip abroad.
ex.zh: 对任何计划出国旅行的人来说，旅行保险都是明智的投资。

senses: v. 投保；给……保险；接受投保；承保；确保
insure.usage: v.为…投保；为…提供保险； 保证，确保；in(否定)+sure(确定)→不确定的事发生时买了保险或有帮助→投保；vt.确保例为2018年新题型；索引p411

ex.en: The painting is insured for $1 million.
ex.zh: 这幅油画投了100万美元的保险。

ex.en: Almost all of the interior detail is of cast iron or plaster; the use of wood was minimized to insure fire safety.
ex.zh: 几乎所有的室内装饰都采用了铸铁或石膏；为了确保消防安全，木材的使用被最小化。

ex.en: The company insures its ships against storms and other risks at sea.
ex.zh: 公司为其船只投保，以防范风暴和其他海上风险。

senses: a. 完好无损的；完整的
a. 完整无缺的；未受损伤的
adj. 原封不动的，未受损伤的
intact.usage: 【记】这座古庙保存完好。；in（表示否定）+tact（接触）→没有接触→我没碰你的东西，它还是“完好无损”的。；索引p411

ex.en: The bridge remains intact even after 30 years.
ex.zh: 虽然过了30年，这座桥还保持完好。

ex.en: The ancient manuscripts were discovered intact, protected by the dry desert air.
ex.zh: 这些古老的手稿被发现时完好无损，是干燥的沙漠空气保护了它们。

ex.en: Despite the fierce competition, the small firm kept its independence intact.
ex.zh: 尽管竞争激烈，这家小公司仍完好地保持着独立。

ex.en: Her sense of humour remained intact despite years of hardship.
ex.zh: 尽管历经多年艰辛，她的幽默感依然未减。

senses: n. 吸入,进气;(气体、液体等)输入口;摄入量;招生人数
n. 摄取量；纳入的人数；吸收
adj. 无形的；难以理解的
adj. 构成整体所必需的
adj. 构成整体所必需的，基本的
v. (使)加入,融入群体;使完全,使完善
v. 使合并，使一体化；使加入
integrate.usage: incorporate 的近义词；【记】理论应与实践相结合。派integration n.结合；融合；inte(发音类似"音体")+grate(发音类似great"好")→音乐体育都要好，全面发展→使一体化；索引p411

ex.en: As many took on the duty of trying to integrate reasoning and scientific philosophies into the world, the Renaissance was over and it was time for a new era.
ex.zh: 当许多人主动承担起将推理和科学哲学融入世界的责任之时,文艺复兴结束了,新的时代由此开启。

ex.en: The department has successfully integrated new ideas into the traditional course structure.
ex.zh: 那个系成功地将新的理念融入传统的课程结构中。

ex.en: As many took on the duty of trying to integrate reasoning and scientific philosophies into the world, the Renaissance was over and it was time for a new era—the Age of Reason.
ex.zh: 当许多人承担责任，试图将推理和科学哲学融入这个世界时，文艺复兴时期就结束了，而要迎来一个新纪元了，那就是理性时代。

phrases.p: the integration of the European community

ex.en: The integration of immigrants into the labour market remains slow.
ex.zh: 移民融入劳动力市场的进程依然缓慢。

ex.en: The integration of digital tools into classrooms has changed how teachers work.
ex.zh: 数字工具融入课堂改变了教师的工作方式。

ex.en: Successful integration requires language training as well as jobs.
ex.zh: 成功的融合既需要工作机会，也需要语言培训。

integrity.usage: 【记】他是一位正直的法官。；n.正直，诚实；完整，完全；索引p411

ex.en: She behaved with absolute integrity.
ex.zh: 她的行为表现绝对正直。

ex.en: Two years ago, Rupert Murdoch's daughter, Elisabeth, spoke of the "unsettling dearth of integrity across so many of our institutions".
ex.zh: 两年前，鲁珀特·默多克的女儿伊丽莎白指出，"令人不安的是，我们的很多机构中都存在诚信缺失的问题"。

ex.en: A judge must have both integrity and the courage to resist outside pressure.
ex.zh: 法官必须既正直，又有抵制外部压力的勇气。

senses: n. 智力；才智超群的人
intellect.usage: n.智力、理解力；知识分子；索引p411

ex.en: Her sharp intellect made short work of problems that puzzled her colleagues.
ex.zh: 她敏锐的智力轻而易举地解决了让同事们困惑的问题。

ex.en: Education should train not only the memory but also the intellect.
ex.zh: 教育应当训练的不仅是记忆力，还有思维能力。

ex.en: He was one of the great intellects of the last century.
ex.zh: 他是上个世纪最伟大的智者之一。

senses: a. 智力的；脑力的；理智的
intellectual.usage: intellect（智力）+u+-al（形容词后缀）→智力的；【记】知识产权应受到保护。；词根记忆:intel(between,之间)+lect(choose,选择)+ual→聪明人在…之间做选择→聪明的；索引p411

ex.en: With the Church's teachings and ways of thinking being eclipsed by the Renaissance, the gap between the Medieval and modern periods had been bridged, leading to new and unexplored intellectual territories.
ex.zh: 教会教义和思维方式因文艺复兴而失势，中世纪和现代之间的鸿沟得以消除，通向尚未探索的新知识领域。

ex.en: The job demands little manual skill but considerable intellectual effort.
ex.zh: 这份工作几乎不需要手工技能，却需要相当的脑力投入。

ex.en: The conference attracted leading intellectuals from across the social sciences.
ex.zh: 这次会议吸引了来自社会科学各领域的顶尖知识分子。

ex.en: Reading widely is the surest path to intellectual growth.
ex.zh: 广泛阅读是智力成长最可靠的途径。

intellectualize.usage: vt.使…有理智；将…作理性研究 vi.诉诸理智；推理

intelligence.usage: intellig（学会）+-ence（名词后缀）→智力；情报；【记】人工智能发展迅速。；n.智力、理解力；情报；索引p411

ex.en: Mr. Mc Whorter, a linguist and controversialist of mixed liberal and conservative professional academic views, sees the triumph of 1960s counter-culture as responsible for the decline of formal English.
ex.zh: McWhorter先生是一位语言学家，也是一位辩论家，其学术观点混合了自由主义与保守主义，他认为20世纪60年代反传统文化运动的胜利导致了规范英语的衰落。

ex.en: Companies are using artificial intelligence to remove some of the unconscious bias from hiring decisions.
ex.zh: 一些公司正利用人工智能来消除招聘决策中的无意识偏差。

ex.en: The agency gathers intelligence from a wide network of sources abroad.
ex.zh: 该机构从广泛的海外情报网收集情报。

ex.en: Tests of general intelligence cannot capture every form of human ability.
ex.zh: 一般智力测试无法涵盖人类能力的所有形式。

senses: a. 有才智的；聪明的；悟性强的
intelligent.usage: intellig（学会）+-ent（形容词后缀）→聪明的；adj.理解力强的、聪明的、智能的；词根记忆: intel(between, 在…之间)+lig(choose, 选择)+ent(形容词后缀)→在两者之间做选择时要有智慧→有智慧的；索引p411

ex.en: Dolphins are widely regarded as among the most intelligent animals in the ocean.
ex.zh: 海豚被普遍认为是海洋中最聪明的动物之一。

ex.en: An intelligent reader questions the evidence behind every bold claim.
ex.zh: 聪明的读者会对每一个大胆论断背后的证据提出质疑。

ex.en: The city has invested in intelligent traffic systems to reduce congestion.
ex.zh: 该市投资建设了智能交通系统以缓解拥堵。

senses: adj. 可理解的,明白易懂的,清楚的
v. 打算，计划，想要；意指
intend.usage: 发音类似“因疼得”→因为肚子疼得受不了了，“打算”去医院检查一下→打算。；词根记忆：in(使…)+tend(倾向)→使想法倾向一边→打算；索引p411

ex.en: I never intended to hurt you.
ex.zh: 我从来都没想伤害你。

ex.en: We accumulate the 50 percent of stuff in our cart that we never intended buying.
ex.zh: 我们把本来根本没打算买的那一半东西推进了购物车。

ex.en: Either Entergy never really intended to live by those commitments, or it simply didn't foresee what would happen next.
ex.zh: 或许安特吉公司从来就没真的打算信守那些承诺，又或许它只是没有预见到接下来会发生什么。

senses: adj. 紧张的；强烈的；热切的；激烈的
adj. 十分强烈的；激烈的；热切的
intense.usage: 真 spark intense opposition 引发强烈反对；索引p411

ex.en: It is sure to spark intense opposition from the far larger number of motorists who will then be affected.
ex.zh: 这肯定会引发更多驾车者的强烈反对，届时他们会受到影响。

ex.en: And since the first Internet gambling site was created in 1995, competition for gamblers' dollars has become intense.
ex.zh: 自1995年第一个网络赌场建立起，对赌徒钱财的争夺战就愈演愈烈。

ex.en: The two teams showed intense competition throughout the final match.
ex.zh: 两队在整场决赛中都展开了激烈的竞争。

senses: adv. 强烈地;紧张地;认真地
adv. 强烈地；紧张地；热情地

ex.en: He remained intensely interested in astronomy throughout his life.
ex.zh: 他一生都对天文学怀有浓厚的兴趣。

ex.en: She was intensely ambitious from an early age.
ex.zh: 她从很小的时候起就雄心勃勃。

ex.en: The final exam season is an intensely stressful time for students.
ex.zh: 期末考试季是学生压力极大的时期。

ex.en: Researchers think that guilt can be a good thing because it may help intensify a child's positive feelings.
ex.zh: 研究人员认为内疚可以是一件好事，因为它可能有助于强化儿童的积极感受。

ex.en: The storm is expected to intensify as it moves towards the coast.
ex.zh: 风暴在向海岸移动的过程中预计会加强。

ex.en: Competition for jobs will intensify as more graduates enter the market.
ex.zh: 随着更多毕业生进入市场，求职竞争将会加剧。

senses: n. 强度；强烈；紧张；剧烈
intensity.usage: 记：in-(加强)+tens(伸)+-ity(名后缀)→光和声能延伸到的尺度→强度；[族]intense a.强烈的；intensify v.（使）增强；真 training intensity 训练强度；索引p411

ex.en: the training intensity
ex.zh: 训练强度

ex.en: Increase time, distance, and intensity gradually.
ex.zh: 逐渐增加时间、距离和强度。

ex.en: The storm lost intensity as it moved inland, sparing the coastal towns.
ex.zh: 风暴在向内陆移动过程中强度减弱，沿海城镇因此幸免。

ex.en: The heat wave reached its peak intensity on Friday afternoon.
ex.zh: 热浪在周五下午达到最强。

senses: a. 加强的；集中的；密集的；集约（经营）的
adj. 加强的,集中的,深入细致的
adj. 密集的；彻底的；集约的
intensive.usage: adj.加强的，集中的；真 labor-intensive crops 劳动密集型作物；索引p411

ex.en: Energy conservation, a shift to other fuels and a decline in the importance of heavy, energy-intensive industries have reduced oil consumption.
ex.zh: 能源节约、燃料替代以及能源密集型重工业的重要性逐渐降低，这些都减少了石油消耗。

ex.en: She took an intensive English course before going to study abroad.
ex.zh: 出国留学前，她参加了一个英语强化课程。

ex.en: The patient needs intensive care in hospital for at least another week.
ex.zh: 病人还需要在医院接受至少一周的重症监护。

senses: n. 打算，计划；意图，目的

phrases.p: have no intention to do sth./of doing sth.

intention.usage: inten(d)（打算）+tion（名词后缀）→意图；n.意图，目的，打算；索引p411

ex.en: A few generative rules are then sufficient to unfold the entire fundamental structure of a language, which is in principle enough to express a whole host of ideas.
ex.zh: 几条生成规则便足以展开一种语言的整个基础结构，这原则上足以表达大量思想。

ex.en: But the intention is not to neglect social science; rather, the complete opposite.
ex.zh: 但其目的并不是要忽视社会科学；而是完全相反。

ex.en: She has no intention of selling her grandmother's old house.
ex.zh: 她无意卖掉祖母的老房子。

senses: adj. 有意的，故意的，存心的

ex.en: It is difficult to prove whether their actions were negligent or intentional.
ex.zh: 很难证明他们的行为是疏忽还是故意的。

ex.en: The referee judged that the foul was intentional and sent the player off.
ex.zh: 裁判认定那次犯规是故意的，将这名球员罚下场。

ex.en: The omission was not intentional; the deadline simply left no time for a full check.
ex.zh: 这一疏漏并非有意为之，只是截止日期太紧，没时间做全面核查。

ex.en: Insurers refused to pay because the damage was clearly intentional.
ex.zh: 保险公司拒绝赔付，因为损坏明显是人为故意造成的。

ex.en: The company was fined for intentionally hiding the safety risks.
ex.zh: 该公司因故意隐瞒安全风险而被罚款。

ex.en: The passage is intentionally vague so that readers can draw their own conclusions.
ex.zh: 这段文字刻意含糊，以便读者自行得出结论。

ex.en: He never intentionally hurts anyone, yet his honesty often offends.
ex.zh: 他从不有意伤害任何人，但他的直率常常冒犯人。

senses: adv. 专心地,专注地;热切地,热心地
vi. 相互作用,相互影响
v. 交流，沟通；相互影响，相互作用
v. 相互作用，相互影响；交流，沟通

phrases.m: adj. 一起活动或互相合作的;交互式的

interact.usage: inter(中间，之间)+act(行动)→两个事物之间不断地有行动→相互作用；索引p411

ex.en: The human systems and the landscapes we live on are linked, and the interactions go both ways.
ex.zh: 人类系统和我们赖以生存的地景是相互联系的，并且双方是相互作用的。

ex.en: Perfume interacts with the skin's natural chemicals.
ex.zh: 香水和皮肤的天然化学物质相互作用。

ex.en: Firms are now studying how genes interact, looking for correlations that might be used to determine the causes of disease or predict a drug's efficacy.
ex.zh: 各公司现在正在研究基因如何相互影响，寻找可能用于确定疾病起因或预测药物疗效的相互关系。

senses: n. 互动，交流；相互作用
interaction.usage: n.互动，交流；相互影响；索引p411

ex.en: Language learning depends on constant interaction with other speakers.
ex.zh: 语言学习依赖于与其他说话者的不断互动。

ex.en: The interaction between diet and exercise is central to the study.
ex.zh: 饮食与运动的相互作用是这项研究的核心。

ex.en: The drug's harmful interaction with alcohol is documented in the report.
ex.zh: 报告记录了该药物与酒精的有害相互作用。

senses: adj. 相互作用的;相互的
n. 相互依赖;相互依存

ex.en: Global trade has created a web of interdependence among the major economies.
ex.zh: 全球贸易在主要经济体之间形成了一张相互依存之网。

ex.en: Ecologists stress the interdependence of plants, animals and soil in a healthy forest.
ex.zh: 生态学家强调健康森林中植物、动物和土壤的相互依存关系。

ex.en: The crisis taught the two countries that their economies rest on mutual interdependence.
ex.zh: 这场危机让两国认识到，它们的经济建立在相互依存之上。

senses: a. 跨学科的；多学科的

ex.en: Britain's new rule is a reminder to bankers that society has an interest in their performance, not just for the short term but for the long term.
ex.zh: 英国的新规定提醒银行家,社会不仅对他们的短期业绩有兴趣,而且对他们的长期业绩也有兴趣。

senses: adj. 有趣的,引人入胜的
n. (两学科等的)相接触并相互影响之处
v. 使连接，使协调，连接；交流，交谈
n. 界面（尤指屏幕布局和菜单）；接口；交接处

phrases.p: the interface between A and B

interface.usage: inter-（相互）+fac（面）+e→呈现在使用者面前的、能实现人机交流的媒介→界面。族interfacial a.界面的；索引p411

ex.en: The new app has a simple interface that older users can master quickly.
ex.zh: 这款新应用界面简单，老年用户也能很快上手。

ex.en: The interface between science and policy is where many disputes arise.
ex.zh: 科学与政策的交汇之处正是许多争议产生的地方。

ex.en: The printer connects to any computer through a standard interface.
ex.zh: 这台打印机通过标准接口与任何电脑相连。

interfere.usage: inter（在……之间）+fer（带来）+e→带到中间→干涉；intervene 的近义词；扩 interfering a. 管闲事的；近 intervene vi. 干涉；干预；in-+ter+fer（带来）+e→把（自己的观点）强行带到他人事务中→干涉。interfere in干预；interfere with妨碍

ex.en: It is not easy to talk about the role of the normal science... without interferring with the normal operation of science.
ex.zh: 谈论常规科学的作用……而不干扰科学的正常运行是不容易的。

ex.en: The police are very unwilling to interfere in family problems.
ex.zh: 警方很不情愿插手家庭问题。

ex.en: Playing computer games late at night can interfere with your sleep and study.
ex.zh: 深夜玩电脑游戏会影响你的睡眠和学习。

senses: n. 无线电信号的干扰
interference.usage: 记 inter-(中间)+fer(拿)+-ence(名词后缀)→把障碍物拿到中间扰乱对方计划→干涉；n.干涉，干预；干扰；索引p411

ex.en: The number of women on corporate boards has been steadily increasing without government interference.
ex.zh: 在没有政府干预的情况下，公司董事会中女性人数占比一直处于稳步上升的状态。

ex.en: Any interference in the judiciary's work would undermine public confidence in the courts.
ex.zh: 任何对司法工作的干涉都会削弱公众对法院的信任。

ex.en: A thunderstorm caused interference with the radio signal for several hours.
ex.zh: 雷暴造成无线电信号干扰了好几个小时。

ex.en: The channel changed its editorial policy under political interference.
ex.zh: 该频道在政治干预下改变了编辑方针。

senses: a. 暂时的；过渡时期的
a. 暂时的；临时的；过渡期间的
interim.usage: 词根inter（在……之间）+im→介于两时间点之间→间歇。临时措施an interim measure；索引p411

ex.en: An interim government will run the country until elections are held.
ex.zh: 临时政府将管理国家，直至举行选举。

ex.en: In the interim, staff will continue to report to their current managers.
ex.zh: 在此期间，员工将继续向现任主管汇报。

ex.en: The committee published interim findings ahead of the final report.
ex.zh: 委员会在最终报告发布前公布了阶段性调查结果。

senses: n. 内部,内地,内陆;内景
n. 内部；里面；内地；内陆；内政
adj. 内部的；内陆的；内政的
interior.usage: adj.内部的 n.内部；内陆，内地；拓展：the interior of a plate 一个板块的内部；索引p411

ex.en: The original interior of the hotel has been replaced.
ex.zh: 旅馆原来的内部装潢已经更换掉了。

ex.en: The interior of the cathedral is decorated with frescoes dating back five centuries.
ex.zh: 大教堂内部装饰着距今五个世纪的壁画。

ex.en: Much of the country's interior remains unexplored because of dense forest.
ex.zh: 由于森林茂密，该国内陆大部分地区仍未被勘探。

ex.en: The interior design of the office uses warm colours to reduce stress.
ex.zh: 办公室的室内设计采用暖色调来缓解压力。

senses: adj. 中间的,居间的;中级的
adj. 中间的，之间的；中级的
intermediate.usage: 助记:inter(在……之间)+medi(中间)+ate(形容词兼名词后缀)→中间的；inter（在……之间）+media（媒体）+te→在媒体之间的→中间的

ex.en: Fewer than half of Americans say they cook at an intermediate level and only 20% describe their cooking skills as advanced.
ex.zh: 不到一半的美国人说他们的烹饪水平是中等的，而只有20%的人说他们有高超的烹饪技术。

senses: a. 间歇的；断断续续的
adj. 间歇的,断断续续的
adj. 间歇的；断断续续的
intermittent.usage: inter-（之间）+mit（送）+-t+-ent（形容词后缀）→被暂时送走一段时间的→间歇的。副词intermittently ad.间歇地；助记:inter(在……之间)+mitt(送)+ent(形容词后缀)→在中间来回地送→间歇的;同义periodic;反义continual adj.连续的；inter（中间）+

ex.en: The workers had been employed on an intermittent basis for many years.
ex.zh: 这些工人已经断断续续地工作了许多年。

ex.en: The village suffers from an intermittent water supply in the dry season.
ex.zh: 旱季这个村庄的供水时断时续。

ex.en: She felt intermittent pain in her shoulder months after the operation.
ex.zh: 手术后几个月，她的肩膀仍感到间歇性疼痛。

senses: adj. 内心的；国内的，内政的；内部的；体内的
adj. 内部的；国内的；体内的
internal.usage: inter（在……之内）+n+-al（形容词后缀）→内部的；索引p411

ex.en: He accused the US of trying to interfere in his country's internal affairs.
ex.zh: 他指责美国试图干涉他的国家的内政。

ex.en: continual internal opposition // internal editors
ex.zh: 持续的来自内部的反对 // 内部编辑

ex.en: The doctor said the injury was internal and needed further examination.
ex.zh: 医生说这是内伤，需要进一步检查。

international.usage: inter（在……之间）+nation（国家）+-al（形容词后缀）→国际的；索引p411

ex.en: The crisis prompted an international response within days.
ex.zh: 这场危机在几天内就引发了国际社会的反应。

ex.en: The city hosts several international conferences every year.
ex.zh: 该市每年举办多场国际会议。

ex.en: International trade depends on agreed rules and stable currencies.
ex.zh: 国际贸易依赖于公认的规则和稳定的货币。

senses: n. [C] 实习期；（尤指）实习医师期
internship.usage: intern（实习医师）+-ship（名词后缀，表身份、状态）→实习医师的身份/状态→实习期。族intern n.实习生

senses: adj. 人际关系的,人际的

ex.en: According to Jenny Radesky, digital products are designed to better interpersonal relations.
ex.zh: 据珍妮·雷德斯基说，数码产品的设计是为了改善人际关系。

ex.en: Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression.
ex.zh: 安巴迪怀疑，认真思考时他们（指参与者）的关注点是生动但具有误导性的线索，如某些手势或话语，而不是让微妙的信号通过复杂的相互影响形成整体印象。

phrases.p: the way in which people interpret what they see
phrases.m: 人们解读所见事物的方式

interpret.usage: inter（在……之间）+pret（=price 价值）→在两者之间确定价值→解释；口译；inter（互相）+pre（前）+t（联想为talk，说）→站在语言不通的人面前来回地说→翻译，解释对方语言的含义→解释；口译。派生：interpreter；索引p411

ex.en: This success, coupled with later research showing that memory itself is not genetically determined, led Ericsson to conclude that the act of memorizing is far more than intuition. In other words, whatever inborn differences two people may exhibit in their abilities to memorize, those differences are swamped by how well each person encodes the information.
ex.zh: 这一成功，加上后来表明记忆力本身并非由基因决定的研究，使Ericsson得出结论：记忆行为远非直觉。换言之，无论两个人在记忆能力上表现出何种先天差异，这些差异都会被每个人对信息编码的出色程度所淹没。

ex.en: One could interpret much of the work of Beethoven by saying that suffering is inevitable, but the courage to fight it renders life worth living.
ex.zh: 我们可以这样解释贝多芬的大部分作品:苦难是不可避免的,但是与苦难抗争的勇气使得生命值得继续。

ex.en: I didn't know whether to interpret her silence as acceptance or refusal.
ex.zh: 我不知该把她的沉默看作接受还是拒绝。

interpretation.usage: n.解释，理解；说明；表演， 演绎；索引p411

ex.en: The contract was ambiguous, and each side offered its own interpretation.
ex.zh: 合同含糊不清，双方各自给出了自己的解释。

ex.en: Her interpretation of the data challenged assumptions long held in the field.
ex.zh: 她对数据的解读挑战了该领域长期持有的假设。

ex.en: The pianist's interpretation of the concerto surprised even longtime fans.
ex.zh: 这位钢琴家对协奏曲的演绎连资深乐迷都感到惊讶。

interpreter.usage: n.口译者，译员；表演者；interpret 的派生词

ex.en: The negotiations proceeded slowly because an interpreter had to translate every sentence.
ex.zh: 谈判进展缓慢，因为口译员要翻译每一句话。

ex.en: She worked as an interpreter at the international court for a decade.
ex.zh: 她在国际法庭担任了十年口译员。

ex.en: A skilled interpreter conveys tone as well as words.
ex.zh: 出色的口译员不仅传达词语，也传达语气。

senses: adj. 省际的;省与省之间的
interprovincial.usage: 词根记忆：inter(between,在…之间)+provinc(e)(省份)+ial(形容词后缀)→省际的。；索引p411

phrases.p: understand the interrelations of man and nature
phrases.m: 理解人和自然的相互关系

senses: v. 打断，打扰；遮挡；使中断
interrupt.usage: inter（在……之间）+rupt（断裂）→在中间断裂→打断；助记:inter(在……之间)+rupt(断裂)→从两者之间断裂→中断；v.打断，打扰；使暂停，使中 断；阻断，遮挡；inter（在……中间）+rupt（=break，断裂，破裂）→在讲话中间断裂→打断。派生：interruption；词根记忆: inter

ex.en: After Hurricane Katrina interrupted routine delivery, temporary mail service points were set up.
ex.zh: 卡特里娜飓风中断了日常投递后，建立了临时邮件服务点。

ex.en: It is not simply that one is interrupted; it is that one is actually inclined to interruption.
ex.zh: 不单纯是思维受到干扰的问题；而是这种思维实际上更倾向于受干扰。

ex.en: Please do not interrupt the speaker while she is making her points.
ex.zh: 发言人陈述观点时请不要打断她。

interruption.usage: n.打断，暂停；中断期；interrupt 的派生词；索引p411

ex.en: His sudden interruption makes me feel outraged.
ex.zh: 他的突然打断使我感到愤怒。

ex.en: The storm caused an interruption in power supplies across the whole region.
ex.zh: 风暴造成整个地区的电力供应中断。

ex.en: He completed the lecture without interruption, despite the noisy crowd outside.
ex.zh: 尽管外面人群嘈杂，他还是没有中断地讲完了课。

ex.en: Apologising for the interruption, she asked the speaker to continue.
ex.zh: 她为打断道歉，请演讲者继续。

senses: n. [C] 交叉路口；十字路口

phrases.p: at the intersection of A and B

intersection.usage: inter-（相互）+sect（切）+-ion（名词后缀）→相互切过的地方→交叉点。族intersect vi.相交 vt.横断；助记:inter(在……之间)+section(截面)→两者之间的截面→交叉点

senses: n.（时间上的）间隔，间歇；幕间休息
interval.usage: inter（在……之间）+val→介于其间的间隔；inter（在……中间）+val（可以联想成wall“墙”）→中间有道墙→间隔。拓展：at (...) intervals 每隔……时间，间或

ex.en: There will be an interval of 20 minutes after the second act.
ex.zh: 第二幕结束后将休息20分钟。

ex.en: Buses to the airport run at intervals of thirty minutes.
ex.zh: 开往机场的巴士每隔三十分钟一班。

ex.en: He returned to the stage after a long interval to loud applause.
ex.zh: 阔别舞台许久后，他在热烈的掌声中重返舞台。

senses: v. 斡旋，调停；介入；干扰；插话
intervene.usage: inter-（之间）+ven（来）→来到中间→介入。近义：interfere vi. 干涉；辨析：与 interfere 均指干扰；intervene 强调介入；interrupt 强调打断；v.干预，干涉；干扰；介于中间；inter（在……中间）+vene（发音类似went“走”）→在中间来来回回地走→斡旋，调停；索

ex.en: She went over to intervene between the two men.
ex.zh: 她走过去为两个男人进行调解。

ex.en: But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that "the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service," and said Congress or the Supreme Court could intervene to "avoid trapping Internet regulation in technological anachronism."
ex.zh: 但法官帕特里夏·米勒特在一份协同意见书中指出：“这一结果与现代宽带服务的实际情况出现了脱节”，并表示国会或最高法院可以进行干预，以“避免使互联网监管陷入技术过时的尴尬境地”。

ex.en: The central bank was forced to intervene to stop the currency falling further.
ex.zh: 央行被迫进行干预，以阻止货币进一步下跌。

senses: n. [U,C] （对他国事务的）介入，干预，干涉行为
intervention.usage: 真 government intervention 政府介入；索引p411

ex.en: Military intervention in the region would risk a wider war.
ex.zh: 对该地区的军事干预将冒引发更大规模战争的风险。

ex.en: Early intervention can prevent minor reading difficulties from becoming serious.
ex.zh: 早期干预能防止轻微的阅读困难变得严重。

ex.en: The central bank's intervention kept the currency from falling further.
ex.zh: 央行的干预阻止了该货币进一步下跌。

senses: n. 接见,会见;采访;面试
interview.usage: 助记:inter(互相间)+view(看)→相互间看→面试；n./v.面试、采访；派生：interviewer；interviewee；索引p411

ex.en: Almost everyone who was interviewed for this special report said that the biggest problem at the moment is not a lack of demand but a lack of good work to sell.
ex.zh: 几乎所有接受本期特别报道的受访者都表示，目前最大的问题不是缺少需求，而是缺乏好的产品可供销售。

ex.en: He studied the results of 9,323 MBA interviews conducted by 31 admissions officers.
ex.zh: 他研究了31位招生负责人进行的9323次MBA面试的结果。

ex.en: She arrived early for her job interview to make a calm, confident impression.
ex.zh: 她提前到达参加求职面试，以便留下冷静自信的印象。

senses: n. 参加面试者;接受采访者
n. 被采访者，接受面试者
n. 参加面试者；接受采访者
interviewee.usage: n.被面试官，被采访者；interview 的派生词；索引p411

ex.en: The interviewee paused before answering, choosing each word with care.
ex.zh: 受访者停顿了一下才回答，字斟句酌。

ex.en: Each interviewee was promised anonymity before the survey began.
ex.zh: 调查开始前，每位受访者的匿名身份都得到了保证。

ex.en: A confident interviewee is more likely to leave a favourable impression on the panel.
ex.zh: 自信的面试者更可能给面试小组留下好印象。

senses: n. 主持面试者;采访者
n. 主持面试者，采访者
n. 采访者；主持面试者
interviewer.usage: n.面试官，采访者；interview 的派生词；索引p411

ex.en: The interviewer asked pointed questions about the company's environmental record.
ex.zh: 采访者就该公司的环保记录提出了尖锐的问题。

ex.en: A skilled interviewer knows when to press and when to stay silent.
ex.zh: 老练的采访者知道何时追问、何时沉默。

ex.en: The interviewer explained that the final decision would be announced within a week.
ex.zh: 面试官解释说，最终决定将在一周内公布。

ex.en: The letters reveal an unexpected intimacy between the two writers.
ex.zh: 这些书信揭示了两位作家之间意想不到的亲密关系。

ex.en: Technology gives an illusion of intimacy while keeping people apart.
ex.zh: 技术在把人隔开的同时给人带来亲密的假象。

ex.en: Decades of working together had created a rare intimacy of understanding.
ex.zh: 数十年的共事造就了一种难得的心意相通。

senses: adj. 亲密的，亲近的；私人的
intimate.usage: inti(在心里面)+mate(人)→能放在心里的人→亲密的；intimate friends密友；索引p411

ex.en: We're not on intimate terms with our neighbours.
ex.zh: 我们和邻居往来不多。

ex.en: Dr. Kroo points out that the aircraft could be separated by several nautical miles, and would not be in the intimate groupings favored by display teams like the Red Arrows.
ex.zh: 克鲁博士指出，飞机之间可以相隔几海里，并不会像诸如“红箭”等飞行表演队所喜欢的那样紧密编队飞行。

ex.en: The small restaurant offers an intimate atmosphere perfect for a quiet dinner.
ex.zh: 这家小餐馆提供温馨私密的氛围，非常适合安静的晚餐。

senses: v. 恐吓,威胁(某人做某事)
intimidate.usage: v.恫吓，威胁；adj.害怕的；受到恐吓的；只会欺负和威胁(intimidate)胆小的(timid)人；派生intimidation n.威胁；索引p411

ex.en: It's more likely to be associated with dominance or intimidation in adversarial situations.
ex.zh: 在敌对场合，它更可能与控制或恐吓有关。

ex.en: Some managers use complex jargon to intimidate junior staff into silence.
ex.zh: 一些管理者用复杂的行话吓唬初级员工，使他们不敢发言。

ex.en: The witness refused to be intimidated by the defence lawyer's aggressive questions.
ex.zh: 证人没有被告方律师咄咄逼人的提问吓住。

ex.en: Tall fences and warning signs failed to intimidate the determined trespassers.
ex.zh: 高高的围栏和警告标志都没能吓退执意闯入者。

senses: prep. 到……里面；进入；朝；向；对着；撞上

intricacy.usage: n.错综复杂的事物；盘根错节；索引p411

ex.en: Visitors marvelled at the intricacy of the palace's carved ceilings.
ex.zh: 游客们对宫殿雕花天花板的精巧繁复赞叹不已。

ex.en: Few outsiders understand the intricacy of the country's tax code.
ex.zh: 局外人很少了解该国税法的错综复杂。

ex.en: The novel captures the intricacy of family relationships in a small village.
ex.zh: 这部小说捕捉到了小村庄里家庭关系的错综复杂。

senses: a. 错综复杂的；复杂精细的
adj. 错综复杂的,复杂精细的
adj. 难理解的,难分析的
adj. 复杂精细的；错综复杂的
intricate.usage: in-（进入）+tric（纠缠）+ate→纠缠在一起→复杂的。近义：complicated a. 复杂的；词根记忆:in(里面)+tric(obstacle,障碍)+ate(形容词后缀)→里面存在障碍物的→错综复杂的；索引p411

ex.en: What WhatsApp offered Facebook was an intricate and finely detailed web of its users' friendships and social lives.
ex.zh: WhatsApp为脸书提供的是其用户复杂又详尽的朋友关系和社交生活网。

ex.en: The watch contains an intricate mechanism of more than two hundred tiny parts.
ex.zh: 这块手表内部有一个由两百多个微小零件组成的精密复杂机构。

ex.en: Negotiating the trade agreement proved far more intricate than either side expected.
ex.zh: 事实证明，谈判这项贸易协定远比双方预期的复杂。

ex.en: She spent months restoring the intricate carvings on the old cathedral door.
ex.zh: 她花了几个月修复古老教堂门上精美的复杂雕饰。

senses: v. 激起某人的兴趣或好奇心
n. 密谋策划；阴谋,秘密安排
adj. (由于奇特、神秘或出人意料而)非常有趣的

phrases.m: 一个非常有趣且重要的问题

senses: adj. (指价值或性质)固有的,内在的,本质的
adj. 固有的，内在的，本身的
intrinsic.usage: 派生intrinsically adv.内在地,本质上；in（里面）+trins（发音类似纯的）+ic→他的内心是非常纯洁的→内在的；索引p411

ex.en: Birds should continue as a matter of intrinsic right, regardless of the presence or absence of economic advantage to us.
ex.zh: 无论鸟类能否给我们带来经济价值，它们自有生存下去的权利。

ex.en: intrinsic right
ex.zh: 与生俱来的权利

ex.en: Reading has intrinsic value beyond its usefulness for exams.
ex.zh: 阅读具有超越应试功用的内在价值。

senses: adv. 本质地；内在地；固有地
v. 闯入,侵入,打搅,把观点等强加于他人

phrases.p: intrude on the federal's privileged powers

intrude.usage: in-（进入）+trud（推）+e→推着进入→闯入。族intruder n.入侵者；intrusion n.侵入；干扰；派生intruder n.闯入的人或物；in（进入）+trud（推，冲）+e→推进去，冲进去→侵入；索引p411

ex.en: Arizona had thus intruded on the federal's priviledged powers.
ex.zh: 亚利桑那州因此侵犯了联邦政府的优先权。

ex.en: Reporters should not intrude on the grief of families who have just lost relatives.
ex.zh: 记者不应打扰刚刚失去亲人的家庭的哀伤。

ex.en: Tall new towers may intrude on the famous view from the historic bridge.
ex.zh: 高耸的新楼可能会破坏这座历史名桥的著名景观。

ex.en: He apologized for intruding, saying he had not realized the office was private.
ex.zh: 他为自己贸然闯入道歉，说自己不知道这间办公室不对外开放。

phrases.p: make a case on one's intuitions
phrases.m: 凭某人的直觉来做出解释

intuition.usage: [族]intuitive a. 直觉的；[近]instinct n. 直觉；in-（不）+tui（看）+-tion（名词后缀）→不用看就知道→直觉。族intuitive a.直觉的；凭直觉得到的；派生intuitive adj.直觉的,来自直觉的；索引p411

ex.en: Experienced doctors often rely on intuition when test results are unclear.
ex.zh: 在检查结果不明确时，经验丰富的医生常常依靠直觉。

ex.en: Her intuition told her that the deal was too good to be true.
ex.zh: 她的直觉告诉她，这笔交易好得让人难以置信。

ex.en: Economic models cannot fully replace the intuition of seasoned policymakers.
ex.zh: 经济模型无法完全取代资深决策者的直觉。

ex.en: Sriri Pillay, an assistant professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School, believes this counter-intuitive link between downtime and productivity may be due to the way our brains operate.
ex.zh: 哈佛医学院的一位名叫西里里·皮莱的精神病学助教认为，停工休息和生产效率之间这种违反直觉的关联可能是由我们大脑的运转方式导致的。

senses: v. 侵略；侵袭；入侵；涌入
invade.usage: 助记:in(进入)+vad(走)+e→侵入；派生invader n.入侵者；in（进入）+vad（走，行）+e→走进去→侵略

ex.en: Demonstrators invaded the government buildings.
ex.zh: 大批示威者闯进了政府办公大楼。

senses: n. 病人,病弱者,伤残人
adj. 有病的,伤残的；供病人用的
adj. (法律上)无效的,作废的;(论据、结论)站不住脚的
adj. 不承认的；无效的；无充分事实的；站不住脚的
invalid.usage: 作形容词读[ˌɪnˈvælɪd]：in-（不）+val（价值）+-id→没有价值的→无效的；作名词读[ˈɪnvəliːd]：需要别人照顾的人→病人；adj.无效的；站不住脚的；不 能识别的 n.病弱者，伤残者；in（表否定）+val（=value，价值）+id（……的）→没有价值的→无效的，作废的。；索引p411

ex.en: Now the company is suddenly claiming that the 2002 agreement is invalid because of the 2006 legislation.
ex.zh: 现在，该公司突然声称，由于2006年的立法，2002年的协议无效。

ex.en: Without the correct signature, the contract is invalid.
ex.zh: 没有正确的签名，这份合同无效。

ex.en: This old ticket is now invalid and cannot be used on high-speed trains.
ex.zh: 这张旧票现在已作废，不能用于乘坐高速列车。

senses: vt. 使无效；证明……错误；使站不住脚
v. 证明……错误,使站不住脚,使无效,使作废
invalidate.usage: in-（不）+valid（有效）+ate→使无效。反义：validate vt. 使有效；v.驳斥，证明是谬误的；使无 效，使作废；索引p411

ex.en: In effect, the White House claimed that it could invalidate any otherwise legitimate state law that it disagrees with.
ex.zh: 实际上，白宫宣称它有权宣布废除任何其不赞同的原本合法的州法律。

ex.en: A single counting error was enough to invalidate the entire set of test results.
ex.zh: 一个计数错误就足以使整组测试结果无效。

ex.en: The missing signature invalidated the contract before it ever took effect.
ex.zh: 缺少签名使这份合同还未生效就作废了。

ex.en: Entering the laboratory without authorisation will invalidate the test conditions.
ex.zh: 未经授权进入实验室会使测试条件失效。

senses: adj. 非常宝贵的,无价的
ad. 始终如一地；一贯地
invariably.usage: in-（不）+vari（变化）+-ably（副词后缀）→不变地→始终如一地。族invariable a.不变的；恒定的

ex.en: The museum was built on the ruins of a fort destroyed during the Roman invasion.
ex.zh: 这座博物馆建在一座毁于罗马入侵的堡垒废墟之上。

ex.en: The sudden invasion of tourists has changed the character of the island.
ex.zh: 游客的突然涌入改变了这个岛的特色。

ex.en: The country promised to respond to any invasion of its territory.
ex.zh: 该国承诺对任何对其领土的入侵作出回应。

senses: vt. 发明；创造；编造；捏造；虚构
v. 发明；创造；虚构；编造
invent.usage: in(里面)+vent(联想went"走")→往学问里面走即钻研→钻研时可能"发明"东西；索引p411

ex.en: When one of these noneconomic categories is threatened and, if we happen to love it, we invent excuses to give it economic importance.
ex.zh: 当某种没有经济效益的物种的生存受到威胁，而我们又恰巧喜欢它时，我们就会找理由赋予它某种经济价值。

ex.en: He did not invent the technology, but he was the first to market it successfully.
ex.zh: 这项技术并非他发明，但他第一个成功将其推向市场。

ex.en: Journalists accused the official of inventing details to make the story more dramatic.
ex.zh: 记者们指责这名官员捏造细节，使报道更具戏剧性。

ex.en: Early civilisations invented writing systems to record trade and taxes.
ex.zh: 早期文明发明了文字系统来记录贸易和税收。

senses: n. 发明；发明物；创造能力；编造

ex.en: the invention of the electric light bulb
ex.zh: 电灯泡的发明

ex.en: The printing press is often ranked among the inventions that changed the world.
ex.zh: 印刷机常被列为改变世界的发明之一。

ex.en: The whole tale of the hidden treasure turned out to be a pure invention.
ex.zh: 关于隐藏财宝的整个故事原来纯属虚构。

ex.en: His latest invention can convert plastic waste into building material.
ex.zh: 他的最新发明能把塑料垃圾转化为建筑材料。

senses: n. 有发明创造能力,独创性
n. 创造性；发明的才能
inventiveness.usage: n.创造性；发明的才能；索引p411

ex.en: The toy's success reflects the inventiveness of its young designer.
ex.zh: 这款玩具的成功反映了其年轻设计师的创造力。

ex.en: Economic hardship often forces a display of popular inventiveness.
ex.zh: 经济困难常常逼出民间的创造性。

ex.en: The award celebrates inventiveness in solving everyday problems.
ex.zh: 该奖项表彰在解决日常问题上的创造力。

senses: n. 发明者,发明家,创造者

ex.en: The inventor spent years perfecting a cheap water filter.
ex.zh: 这位发明家花了数年完善一种廉价的滤水器。

ex.en: Edison is remembered as the inventor of the practical electric lamp.
ex.zh: 爱迪生作为实用电灯的发明者被人们铭记。

ex.en: The young inventor patented her design before the exhibition opened.
ex.zh: 这位年轻发明家在展览开幕前为她的设计申请了专利。

senses: n. [C] 详细目录；存货清单
v. 列出清单,编入目录,存盘
n. 详细目录,清单,存货
inventory.usage: in-（进入）+vent（来）+-ory（名词后缀，表地点）→进来的货物都记录在案的地方→库存清单；索引p411

ex.en: The store keeps a complete inventory of everything on its shelves.
ex.zh: 这家商店对货架上的所有商品都有完整的存货清单。

ex.en: Slow sales left the factory with a huge inventory of unsold goods.
ex.zh: 销售不畅使工厂积压了大量未售出的库存。

ex.en: Managers use software to track inventory in real time.
ex.zh: 经理们使用软件实时跟踪库存。

senses: adj. 相反的,反向的,翻转的,倒转的
n. 反数,倒数,相反,颠倒
inverse.usage: 派生 inversely adv. 相反地；inversion n. 倒置,颠倒

senses: vt. 使反向,使倒转,使颠倒
invert.usage: in-（进入）+vert（转）→向里/反向转→倒置。倒装句语法术语inversion n.倒装；倒转；族inverse a.相反的；同义：reverse, overturn；in（里面）+vert（转变，改变）→从里面转变，彻底改变→颠倒；词根记忆：in(against,反)+vert(turn,转变)→转向反方向→使

ex.en: The traditional rule was it's safer to stay where you are, but that's been fundamentally inverted.
ex.zh: 传统的规则是留在原处更加安全，但那个规则已经被彻底颠覆了。

ex.en: To read the negative, photographers once had to invert light and dark.
ex.zh: 在过去，摄影师要看懂底片就得把明暗颠倒过来。

ex.en: If you invert the order of the two steps, the experiment fails completely.
ex.zh: 如果把这两个步骤的顺序颠倒过来，实验就会完全失败。

ex.en: This lens inverts the image, so the scene appears upside down in the viewfinder.
ex.zh: 这种镜头会使图像倒转，因此在取景器里场景是上下颠倒的。

ex.en: The company decided to invest heavily in research and development.
ex.zh: 公司决定在研发方面进行大量投资。

ex.en: Many parents invest in their children's education from an early age.
ex.zh: 许多父母从孩子幼年起就在其教育上投资。

ex.en: He invested all his savings in the stock market and lost most of them.
ex.zh: 他把全部积蓄投进股市，损失了大半。

investigate.usage: invest(投资)+i(我)+gate(门口)→投资前，我站在门口先"调查，研究"一下；拆分记忆：invest(投资)+i+gate(大门)→investigate；索引p411

ex.en: The researchers investigated one class sessions' impact on eating meat.
ex.zh: 研究人员调查了一堂课对吃肉行为的影响。

ex.en: Police are investigating the cause of the fire that destroyed the warehouse.
ex.zh: 警方正在调查烧毁仓库的那场大火的原因。

ex.en: Scientists investigated the effects of the new drug on patients of different ages.
ex.zh: 科学家研究了这种新药对不同年龄患者的影响。

investigation.usage: n.调查；研究；investigate 的派生词；辨析：investigation 侧重指调查真相或详细研究，常译为"调查；审查"；索引p411

ex.en: Starting next year, any guaranteed bonus of top executives could be delayed 10 years if their banks are under investigation for wrongdoing.
ex.zh: 从明年开始，如果银行因为不法行为而受到调查，那么任何承诺给银行高管的奖金会推迟十年发放。

ex.en: It is under the FCC's investigation.
ex.zh: 它（指美国电话电报公司）正在接受美国联邦通信委员会(FCC)的调查。

ex.en: The police opened an investigation into the cause of the fire.
ex.zh: 警方对火灾起因展开了调查。

senses: n. 投资；投资金额；（时间、精力的）投入
investment.usage: n.投资；（时间、精力的）投入；n.投资；投入；n.投资例为2021年阅读；索引p411

ex.en: If unable to calm down passengers, the railways may have to face the loss of investment.
ex.zh: 如果不能让乘客冷静下来，铁路可能不得不面临投资损失。

ex.en: Education is an investment that pays dividends for both individuals and society.
ex.zh: 教育是一种对个人和社会都有回报的投资。

ex.en: The country attracted record levels of foreign investment after simplifying its tax code.
ex.zh: 简化税制后，该国吸引了创纪录的外国投资。

ex.en: Even a modest investment in insulation can cut heating bills sharply.
ex.zh: 即使在保温上投入不多，也能大幅削减取暖费用。

investor.usage: n.投资者，投资机构；invest 的派生词；索引p411

ex.en: Investors fled the market after the central bank raised interest rates unexpectedly.
ex.zh: 央行出人意料地加息后，投资者纷纷逃离市场。

ex.en: A cautious investor spreads risk across different industries and regions.
ex.zh: 谨慎的投资者会把风险分散到不同的行业和地区。

ex.en: The startup convinced investors that its technology could cut energy costs in half.
ex.zh: 这家初创公司让投资者相信，其技术能将能源成本降低一半。

senses: adj. 无形的；看不见的；隐身的

ex.en: Germs are invisible to the naked eye, yet they shape human history in profound ways.
ex.zh: 细菌肉眼看不见，却深刻地塑造着人类历史。

ex.en: Many carers remain invisible to statistics because their work is unpaid.
ex.zh: 许多照护者在统计中是隐形的，因为他们的工作没有报酬。

ex.en: The ink made the message invisible until it was held near a flame.
ex.zh: 这种墨水使字迹隐去，直到靠近火焰才显现。

senses: v. 援引,援用(法律、规则等)

ex.en: Both of these books are published next week by Penguin Random House, a company currently involved in a stand-off with Waterstones.
ex.zh: 这两本书都将在下周由企鹅兰登书屋出版,该公司目前正与水石陷入对峙。

ex.en: Fantasies of great wealth often involve visions of fancy cars and extravagant homes.
ex.zh: 说起巨额财富，人们往往会想到名车（豪车）与豪宅。

ex.en: The new job involves travelling to branch offices twice a month.
ex.zh: 这份新工作需要每月两次前往分部办事处出差。
